title: Lively stream schemas & tool tiling — PRD (wip)
content:
Purpose and short pitch:
This doc proposes a low-friction incremental output model ("lively schemas") + a "tool tiling" runtime pattern for Hosted API to optimize low-latency partial-results, structured tool calls, and predictable SDK ergonomics for embedded clients. Goal: enable clients to receive useful structured fragments quickly (under 50–120ms first-byte on typical flows) while supporting robust tool orchestration and clear upgrade/downgrade behaviors when network or runtime constraints intervene.

Background / motivation:
- Customers are integrating tool-enabled LLM features into latency-sensitive UI components (autocomplete, IDE helpers, chat widgets). They want early, usable partial outputs rather than a single opaque blob at the end.
- Existing incremental streaming designs at Redwood are powerful but produce monolithic frames or require heavy client parsing. Tool calls complicate things: a tool result is an atomic external dependency but the model may synthesize partial structured hints (e.g., arguments) before the tool resolves.
- SDK authors need a predictable surface: small, composable events rather than ad-hoc fragments. Clients should be able to bind into partial schemas (e.g., summary, candidate list, action frame) and downgrade gracefully if incomplete.

Principles:
1) Event-first: stream is a sequence of typed events (frames) with small JSON-like payloads. Events are intentionally fine-grained to enable responsive UIs.
2) Deterministic reconciliation: each event has a monotonic sequence id + stable event id so SDKs can deduplicate and rehydrate across reconnects.
3) Schema layering: deliver small typed schema shards (e.g., summary.v1, choices.v2, action-args.v1) that compose into larger objects. Each shard declares minimal validation keys.
4) Tool-tiling: treat tool interactions as "tiles" — self-contained tiles include lifecycle hints (pending/resolved/failed), a canonical tool id, and a reference to the schema shard(s) the tool will produce. This keeps parsing and UX wiring simple.
5) Latency-first fallbacks: if tool latencies or capacity constraints are high, the runtime can emit a "tiling-fallback" event (lightweight suggestion or stub) and later patch with the full tile.

User stories:
- As an engineer building an adventure game chat UI, I want token-level narrative fragments and an early list of candidate actions so players get immediate interactivity while final choices load.
- As a platform integrator, I want clear events for tool invocation and result boundaries so I can log, audit, and assert SLAs without re-parsing noisy text.
- As an SDK author, I want small, stable parsing rules so I can provide adapters for web and mobile without heavy client-side parsing logic.

Success metrics (initial):
- 95th percentile first meaningful-frame latency reduced by 20% for sample chat workloads vs. baseline streaming.
- Client-side parsing error rate (schema mismatch) under 1% on canary customers.
- Reduction in tool-related 500s by 30% due to explicit tile lifecycles and fallback rules.

API surface (sketch):
- /v1/responses/stream (existing) — event-mode toggle parameter: event_mode=tiling
- Accepts: model, prompt, tools[], preferred_schema_set (list of shard ids), client_pref (latency|fidelity)
- Stream events (newline-delimited JSON frames). Example frames:
  {"event_type":"init","seq":1,"session_id":"s-123","schemas":["summary.v1","choices.v1"]}  <-- handshake
  {"event_type":"shard","seq":2,"shard_id":"summary.v1","shard_idx":0,"body":"Draft outline text","confidence":0.87}  <-- partial content
  {"event_type":"tile.invoke","seq":3,"tile_id":"tool-geo-01","tool":"geo-resolver","expected_shards":["geo.v1"],"status":"pending"} <-- tool call started
  {"event_type":"shard","seq":4,"shard_id":"choices.v1","choices":[{"id":"c1","text":"Short answer"},{"id":"c2","text":"Longer answer"}],"confidence":0.72} <-- partial choice list
  {"event_type":"tile.result","seq":5,"tile_id":"tool-geo-01","status":"resolved","shards":[{"shard_id":"geo.v1","body":{"lat":...}}]} <-- tile resolved (can be larger)
  {"event_type":"complete","seq":6} <-- final marker
- Important: shard frames are intentionally small (bounded size) and may be emitted multiple times during generation. seq is monotonic, clients must accept re-ordered arrival within same seq window and reconcile by shard_idx and unique ids.

SDK ergonomics notes (web + mobile):
- Provide a small runtime that exposes: onInit(handshake), onShard(shard), onTileUpdate(tileEvent), onComplete().
- Offer adapters: "shard-binding" helpers (bindShardToComponent(shard_id, validator, onPatch)) to let UI components subscribe to a shard id and get incremental patches.
- For low-footprint mobile SDKs, we support a minimal text-only mode where shards are emitted as compact text frames and expanded by a background parse step.

Tool tiling behaviors and guarantees:
- Tile lifecycle: pending -> partial -> resolved | failed. Each transition emits an explicit tile event.
- Atomic resolution: when a tile resolves, its final shards are emitted within a single tile.result event if possible. If size prevents atomic emission, tile.result can provide a continuation reference (tile.continuation_url) and small resume tokens.
- Fallback rule: after X ms (configurable per-customer; default 300ms), if a tile is still pending and client_pref=latency, runtime emits tile.stub containing best-effort hints inferred so far. The SDK should render stubs in a lower-fidelity UI state and replace them on resolution.

Operational and security considerations:
- Traceability: each tile event must include tooling metadata (tool version, region, call_id) for auditing.
- Billing: shard and tile events are billable tokens; introduce "shard_count" in telemetry to map to token units.
- Abuse vectors: make sure tile.continuation_url signatures expire and that stubs don't leak sensitive tool-internal IDs.

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Internal SDK alpha (2 weeks): ship event_mode=tiling behind flag + internal sample clients.
2) Internal canary (4 weeks): route 1% of traffic for a subset of models; collect parsing error telemetry, fallback rates.
3) Beta partners (8–12 weeks): enable on opt-in tenants building latency-sensitive integrations. Provide migration guide and sample adapters.
4) General availability (Q3): enable as stable API with production SLAs and dashboarding.

Open design questions / unresolved tradeoffs:
- How to bound shard frame sizes to avoid fragmentation while keeping shard semantics expressive? Proposal: 8KB soft limit per shard, with an explicit "continuation_token" for larger payloads.
- How to prioritize tile invocation across heterogeneous tool pools (some tools expensive)? Need policy language (tool_priority / honor_budget) tied to tenant quotas.
- How to support resumable sessions across device switches (desktop->mobile)? We need a compact session snapshot event that includes last seq, acknowledged shard ids, and tile states.

Instrumentation and dashboards required:
- First-meaningful-frame (seq <= 2) latency by model & region.
- Tile latency distribution (pending->resolved), tile.stub rates, fallback rate per tenant.
- Schema validation errors (client-side parse failures) by shard id.

Appendix: quick example — client-side parsing loop (pseudocode)
  openStream(params...)
  onEvent(e):
    switch e.event_type:
      case 'init': session = e.session_id
      case 'shard': applyShard(e.shard_id, e.shard_idx, e.body)
      case 'tile.invoke': markTilePending(e.tile_id)
      case 'tile.result': applyTileShards(e.tile_id, e.shards); markTileResolved(e.tile_id)
      case 'tile.stub': showLowFidelity(e.tile_id, e.stub)
      case 'complete': finalize()
Notes to reviewers:
- Focus feedback on: shard sizing policy, tile fallback defaults, and SDK adapter ergonomics.
- If you want to prototype UX quickly, try the sample repo GH:repo/redwood-hosted-api/examples/tiling-demo (linked above).

Next steps (this week):
- Engineering: feasibility spike for tile.atomic emission and continuation tokens (Ethan).
- SDK: simple JS adapter that binds summary.v1 -> document component and choices.v1 -> choice list (Liam).
- Product: finalize default fallback timeout and client_pref semantics (Priya).
